board.name: Kansas State Board of Healing Arts

licence.title: Physician Assistant (PA) license, active designation
licence.renewalDeadline: Annual: license cancelled December 31 each year (a license issued or reinstated October 1 to December 31 runs to December 31 of the following year); renewal window opens November 15; late renewal January 1 to January 31 with late fee; status Cancelled for Failure to Renew on February 1.

ce.categoryRules: Annual option: 50 hours in the preceding year with at least 20 Category I and at least 1 Category III. Two-year option: 100 hours in the preceding two years with at least 40 Category I and at least 2 Category III. Category III = a Category I or II activity on acute or chronic pain management, appropriate opioid prescribing, or use of prescription drug monitoring programs. One hour = 50 minutes. PAs initially licensed within one year of a renewal date are exempt for the first renewal.
ce.acceptsNccpaCertificationInLieu: Not named in the rule. K.A.R. 100-28a-5(a)(3) accepts verification of equivalent hours, in number and category, from a national, state or local organization with standards at least as stringent as the board's.

topicMandates.topic: Category III: acute or chronic pain management, appropriate prescribing of opioids, or use of prescription drug monitoring programs
topicMandates.appliesTo: All PAs renewing (1 hour per year on the 50 hour option; 2 hours on the 100 hour two-year option)

ce.controlledSubstanceCe: Category III hour(s) above; no separate prescriber-only CE found

practice.agreementFilingAndRenewal: Before practicing, file an Active Practice Request form signed by the PA and the supervising physician, containing the written agreement (services, prohibited procedures, supervision types, prescription-only drug authority). Amendments go to the board within 10 days. The supervising physician reviews the form at least annually. Termination of supervision is reported on a board form. A current active practice form and written agreement must be on file.
practice.notes: PAs practice 'in a dependent role with a supervising physician' (K.S.A. 65-28a08). Professional liability insurance and Health Care Stabilization Fund surcharge required for an active license.

upcoming.source: 2026 Kan. Sess. Laws ch. 36 (HB 2702), approved April 3, 2026
upcoming.agreementType: collaboration for PAs attesting 4,000+ postgraduate clinical hours with no discipline; supervision for fewer than 4,000 hours
upcoming.agreementFilingAndRenewal: Collaborating PAs: practice agreement kept on file at the practice site and given to the board on request. PAs under 4,000 hours: physician supervision under a written practice agreement; supervision practice agreements must be provided to the board before practice, and termination is reported on a board form. Act renamed the physician assistant and physician associate licensure act.
upcoming.note: The board's implementing regulations (K.A.R. 100-28a) for the new practice agreements were not loaded; the active practice request form rules below remain in force until January 1, 2027.

prescribing.ceForPrescribers: Prescribing only under the written agreement with the supervising physician; DEA registration required for controlled substances. No separate Kansas controlled substance registration: mid-level practitioners (PAs with prescribing authority under a written agreement) are exempt from Board of Pharmacy registration.

rn.renewalDeadline: Last day of the birth month; renew in odd-numbered years if born in an odd year, even-numbered years if born in an even year; board mails a renewal notice at least 60 days before expiration; a licence that would come due within six months of qualifying expires the last day of the month after the third birthday from licensure.
rn.ceNotes: 30 contact hours of approved CNE in the most recent prior licensing period; no carryover. No CE for the first renewal of a licence that expires within 30 months after the licensure exam, or within the first nine months after licensure by reinstatement or endorsement (K.S.A. 65-1117(a)).

aprn.title: APRN (Advanced Practice Registered Nurse), nurse practitioner role
aprn.separateLicenceOrCertificate: separate APRN license, renewed with a separate application alongside the RN license
aprn.renewalNotes: Same biennial cycle as the RN license (K.A.R. 60-11-113(a)); proof of malpractice insurance at renewal unless an exception applies
aprn.ceNotes: 30 contact hours of approved CNE related to the APRN role; these hours also count toward the RN license renewal. Up to 15 hours may be instructor credit. CME needs individual offering approval (IOA) before renewal.
aprn.nationalCertificationRequired: Required for initial licensure on or after July 1, 2023; APRNs licensed before then may submit it at renewal. Maintenance at each renewal is not stated in the statute or rule.

practice.agreementFilingAndRenewal: None since the 2022 amendment (L. 2022 ch. 65; 2022 S Sub for HB 2279): the statute authorizes APRN prescribing with no collaborative agreement or protocol. Malpractice insurance is required to render clinical services.

unverified: K.A.R. 100-28a-5 and 100-28a-15 were confirmed in the Kansas Register (July 2021) and the KSBHA November 2024 booklet. The official SOS regulation site needs a CAPTCHA, so an amendment after November 2024 is not ruled out.

The KSBHA FAQ says PA licences 'expire on January 31st'. K.A.R. 100-28a-15 says cancelled December 31, and K.S.A. 65-28a03(c) allows renewal with a late fee within the following 30 days. Recorded as a December 31 deadline with a January 1 to 31 late window.
No page loaded says whether KSBHA accepts current NCCPA certification under K.A.R. 100-28a-5(a)(3).

From January 1, 2027 (HB 2702), K.S.A. 65-1626 still defines a PA 'mid-level practitioner' by a 'written agreement with a supervising physician'. Whether collaborating PAs stay exempt from Board of Pharmacy controlled substance registration under K.S.A. 65-4116(c)(8) is not settled by any source loaded.
KSBHA implementing regulations for HB 2702 practice agreements (form, filing, review interval) were not found or loaded.
Neither K.S.A. 65-1130 nor K.A.R. 60-11-113 says Kansas APRNs must keep national certification at each renewal. They require it only for initial licensure on or after July 1, 2023.

'Full' practice authority for Kansas APRNs is inferred: K.S.A. 65-1130 (history ends L. 2022 ch. 65; 2026 statute book) has no collaboration or supervision requirement. The board does not use that label.

The KSBN Nurse Practice Act (December 2025) has no Kansas RN or APRN topic mandates (opioid, implicit bias, trafficking, suicide, dementia); recorded as none. KSBN regulations amended after December 2025 were not checked because of the SOS CAPTCHA.
